name: King's Landing: Rock Springs Run and Emerald Cut
area: 5722 Baptist Camp Road, Apopka, Orange County
coordinateNote: Operator homepage businessLocationCoordinates read directly from its published page data: 28.7684223, -81.5037052. Official river-system map independently places road access at 28.7684, -81.5039.
experience: Paddle the Emerald Cut through clear green water and overhanging forest, with swim stops allowed on the operator's day-paddle route. From King's Landing, the right turn is upstream toward the Kelly Park barrier; turn around there and drift back. The left-hand route offers a different wildlife paddle. A four-hour rental allows both directions; the 8.5-mile shuttle trip is a separate booking.
duration: Guided Emerald Cut 2 hours; longer shuttle run a substantial separate outing.
cost: Operator lists Emerald Cut guided tour $59/person, VIP 2.5-hour trip $89. Own-boat day launch advertised $10/adult, weekend walk-in $20; own-boat shuttle package $30/adult. Confirm booking total.
access: King's Landing publishes 8 a.m.–5 p.m. hours and four-hour self-guided day rentals. Day paddle is out-and-back with no shuttle. The operator permits stopping, swimming and snacks on this route; follow on-site boundaries. The Kelly Park barrier is a turnaround point, not admission to Kelly Park's swimming area.

water: No dated live visibility report established; descriptive clarity is general.
mobility: Upstream effort on Emerald Cut; guided VIP description avoids upstream paddle via forest transport. Boat entry/control required.

name: Coldwater Creek paddle and tube trips (Adventures Unlimited Outdoor Center)
coordinateNote: Entrance or parking coordinates from the November 12, 2026 gap review.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Rent a kayak, canoe, paddleboard or tube and get shuttled upstream, then drift back past white sandbars to Tomahawk Landing. The 11-mile run is the long day; the 4-mile trip is the easy float. The same property has a zipline course and cabins/campsites.
cost: Single kayak from $42 (4 or 7 miles), $53.05 (11 miles); duo kayak from $84; $5 per person walk-on fee without a reservation
access: Reservations and full prepayment required (book online or call 850-623-6197; under 48 hours out, call). Off-season departures: 4-mile on the hour 10 a.m.-1 p.m., 7-mile 9 a.m.-1 p.m., 11-mile 9 a.m. weekdays. Closed Wednesdays Nov 4-Feb 3, Thanksgiving and Christmas.

conditions.summary: Operator site shows only the seasonal Wednesday closure (Nov 4-Feb 3) and lists the river level as GREEN, safe for all. Do not confuse with the Florida Forest Service's separate Coldwater Recreation Area (equestrian), which is still closed after Isaias. (source dated read 2026-11-12)

name: Cobb Hunt Camp (Osceola National Forest)
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Primitive camp between Ocean Pond and Olustee Battlefield with Florida Trail access and a portable toilet during hunt season. No drinking water; Ocean Pond Campground nearby sells showers.
access: No reservation needed. Stay limit: 14 days per month (National Forests in Florida) Forest Service: 'General gun season runs from mid-November to early January' and all camping is then restricted to designated hunt camps and Ocean Pond Campground. Derived from rule text (opens 7 days after the first day of Zone C antlered deer season, closes 57 days later) and FWC's 2026-27 Zone C start of Nov 7: about Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027; the 2026-27 brochure itself was not retrieved. Roadside dispersed camping in Osceola NF is therefore not legal on Nov 21 - Dec 8. Forest Service urges hikers to wear bright colors.
